title: JANUS Engine — Legacy Cryogenic ASU Reference Architecture

provenance.source_type: user-supplied historical workplace photographs plus user recollection
provenance.user_confirmation: The photographed installation separated air into oxygen and nitrogen; nitrogen was used to cool adsorber vessels; a residual/off-gas stream was vented to atmosphere; the installation included the membrane and process elements discussed in the Janus Engine branch.
provenance.candidate_family_context: Older Soviet/post-Soviet cryogenic air-separation equipment of K / KZh / KZhAZh-type family was considered visually and functionally similar, but no exact model identification is asserted by this record.
provenance.evidence_boundary: Functional recollection is stored as user testimony; exact equipment model, piping identifiers and original operating manual remain unverified.

legacy_process_functions: gas separation into oxygen and nitrogen
nitrogen reuse as a cooling and/or regeneration service stream
multiple controlled gas branches with independent flow/pressure indication
off-gas disposal after useful process duty

optimization_lesson.core_observation: The installation is valuable as a reference because its subsystems support one another: product and by-product streams are reused for cooling, regeneration, purification and process stabilization rather than every function requiring an independent energy source.
optimization_lesson.janus_translation: JANUS Engine should be designed as an exergy-cascade and multi-duty flow architecture: each stream is evaluated for additional useful duties before vent, recycle or consumption.
optimization_lesson.non_claim: Process integration can reduce losses and auxiliary demand, but it does not make the plant energetically self-sustaining and does not remove the need for an external energy input and waste-heat sink.

legacy_to_janus_mapping.atmospheric_air_feed: waterborne dissolved-gas feed through rotating artificial gills
legacy_to_janus_mapping.legacy_membrane_or_separation_stage: JANUS rotating-gill membrane plus downstream gas-separation stage
legacy_to_janus_mapping.nitrogen_cooling_of_adsorbers: cold-N2 cooling phase of the ring carousel
legacy_to_janus_mapping.nitrogen_regeneration_or_purge: N2 cascade into regeneration and inert-service duties
legacy_to_janus_mapping.legacy_heat_exchangers: annular recuperator / condenser / water-cooled heat-rejection sections
legacy_to_janus_mapping.moisture_separator: JANUS demister plus moisture condenser and condensate recovery
legacy_to_janus_mapping.oxygen_product: JANUS O2 process stream with optional compression / cryogenic branch only after energy gates pass
legacy_to_janus_mapping.off_gas: last-resort vent after remaining pressure, temperature and inerting utility have been evaluated

nitrogen_candidate_duties: inert barrier between oxygen-rich and hot/mechanical regions
controlled vent or recycle only after prior duties
oxygen_candidate_duties: useful product / oxidizer only after purity and safety requirements are met
optional cryogenic storage branch after water/CO2 removal and energy-budget validation
water_candidate_duties: ultimate heat sink where sufficiently colder than the rejecting surfaces
reoxygenation loop only with explicit O2 mass balance

reference_use_in_branch.method: For each JANUS component, identify the legacy industrial function it replaces, then compare mass flow, energy flow, pressure drop, regeneration duty, cooling duty and safety burden.
reference_use_in_branch.primary_question: Can JANUS preserve the useful process-integration logic of the legacy ASU while changing feed acquisition to dissolved-gas extraction and compressing functions into annular modules?
